items.title: Contentious mayoral race brings Mississauga voters out in high numbers
items.summary: As it turns out, Mississauga’s contentious mayoral race was just the tonic needed to spark greater interest among voters. A 2026 mayoral contest featuring fierce political rivals Carolyn Parrish, the incumbent, and her predecessor Bonnie Crombie helped draw considerably more eligible voters to the polls than turned out in the 2022 Mississauga municipal election. Add to the mix one-term city councillor (and now mayor-elect) Alvin Tedjo who, among other candidates, took on Parrish in the 2024 byelection to succeed a Queen’s Park-bound Crombie, and a recipe for even stronger voter participation came together. Dipika Damerla, on her way out as Mississauga Ward 7 councillor after finishing a distant fourth in Monday’s mayoral contest, rounded out the roster of four high-profile candidates who helped get the votes out. 9 per cent of eligible voters (191,166 voters) cast ballots to elect the mayor, 11 city councillors and a slate of school board trustees. 8 per cent (107,310 voters), among the lowest participation rates in Ontario (see chart below), took part in the process. 7 per cent. 6 per cent of Mississauga voters took part in the election.

items.title: Monday's municipal elections produced many upsets across Ontario, including a career-ending result for Canada's longest-serving mayor
items.summary: Here’s a look at some of southern Ontario’s most notable election results, including incumbent mayor defeats in Milton, Mississauga, Oakville, Hamilton, Niagara Falls and elsewhere. Alvin Tedjo celebrates with supporters on election night after being elected as mayor of Mississauga. Monday’s Ontario municipal election was full of surprises as longtime Milton mayor Gord Krantz lost after more than 40 years as head of the town’s council, while voters also replaced incumbent mayors in Mississauga, Oakville, Hamilton, Niagara Falls and elsewhere. For Toronto, it was status quo as incumbent mayor Olivia Chow overcame an early deficit to comfortably defeat challenger Brad Bradford. It was also an early night for poll watchers in Brampton, as incumbent mayor Patrick Brown won a decisive majority in a field of 12 candidates. Burlington’s Mariane Meed Ward withstood a spirited challenge to retain her job as mayor, despite notable gains for challenger Lisa Kearns, who released a campaign video that went viral prior to election day. Other results were perhaps surprising, including in Mississauga where several experienced political stalwarts were vying for the top job. Here’s a look at some of southern Ontario’s most notable election results, including upsets and a stunning result in Hamilton.

items.title: Street racing in Mississauga leads to list of charges for Toronto man
items.summary: A Toronto man who was prohibited from showing up at car meets and rallies — and any locations where stunt driving may occur — faces multiple charges after a police investigation into street racing and dangerous driving in Mississauga. Peel Regional Police said officers with the force’s Safer Roads Team led the investigation and subsequently made the recent arrest. In the early morning hours of Oct. , officers spotted a vehicle that was engaged in a street race with other cars in the area of Meadowpine Boulevard and Meadowvale Boulevard in the northwest part of the city. “The vehicle was travelling at a high rate of speed and in close proximity to pedestrians, creating a significant risk to public safety,” Peel police said on Tuesday. Investigators identified a suspect and arrested a man on Oct. 15. Anthony Fuellos Knox, 21, of Toronto, is charged with: The accused was released on an undertaking and is scheduled to appear in Ontario Court of Justice in Brampton at a later date, police said. Safer Roads Team officers seized the involved vehicle and suspended the accused’s driver’s licence for 30 days.

items.title: Fireworks rules residents need to know as Diwali approaches in Mississauga
items.summary: Mississauga officials are urging people to follow fireworks rules during upcoming Diwali celebrations after receiving the largest number of complaints in the city’s history during last year’s religious and cultural festival. The City of Mississauga received 432 public complaints related to Diwali fireworks celebrations in the days leading up to, on and after the 2025 Hindu festival of lights, which took place last October. That number was the “highest in history,” Mayor Carolyn Parrish said at the time. Diwali celebrations take place this year from Nov. 6-10, with the main celebratory day falling on Nov. 8. “With Diwali approaching, the City of Mississauga is reminding residents who plan to include fireworks in their celebrations to plan ahead, know the rules and put safety first,” the city said in a notice to residents this week. Under the City of Mississauga’s relatively new fireworks bylaw, family/backyard fireworks can be used on private property with no permit needed from the city only on Nov. m. Fireworks cannot be used on roads, sidewalks, in parking lots or on other public property, the city added, noting a permit is required to use fireworks on another day (other than Nov. 8) or hold a fireworks display at a city park or public place. City officials also said they’ll have extra bylaw enforcement officers on duty during Diwali to enforce rules and educate people on the proper use of fireworks.

items.title: Mother looks for answers after son stabbed with scissors in a Mississauga daycare
items.summary: A Mississauga mother is looking for answers after her four-year-old son was stabbed with scissors in a daycare. Nazli Yilmaz said her son sustained a “deep wound” near his eye requiring stitches after another child allegedly attacked her son while he was at a PLASP after-school care program at Cooksville Creek Public School in Mississauga on Oct. 5. Yilmaz said that despite the severity of her son’s injury, emergency medical services were never contacted. “Staff cleaned him up, changed his bloodied clothing, and waited for me to arrive,” she said. She doesn’t blame the child, who is reportedly non-verbal and has special needs, but instead has concerns about how PLASP handled the incident. “I’m not going to hold a child accountable,” Yilmaz told INSAUGA Canada. “It’s the adults. ” At the same time, she recognizes educators are often underpaid and overworked. But she said there was a lack of information about what happened, why paramedics weren’t called, what type of scissors were used to cause such a deep wound, and how another child was able to get those scissors. She said the answers weren’t forthcoming.

items.title: Ontario's Police Watchdog Clears OPP Officer After Man Fractures Ribs Fleeing Cannabis Search on Highway 407
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Ontario's Special Investigations Unit has closed its probe into a Highway 407 traffic stop after determining a man's fractured ribs were not caused by police. According to the outlet, an OPP officer pulled over a westbound vehicle near Mavis Road on the morning of Oct. 11 for a Highway Traffic Act violation and then found an unsealed bag of suspected cannabis on the front console. The SIU says that while the officer searched the trunk, a 36-year-old passenger climbed over the highway guardrail and ran down an embankment, where he tripped and fell. The agency reports the man was taken to the detachment, where he complained of chest pain and difficulty breathing. According to SIU Deputy Director Stacey O'Brien, a review of video footage confirmed no force was used by police beyond handcuffing him during the arrest, and the man's injuries resulted from his own fall while trying to flee.

items.title: First Mayor in Nearly 50 Years With No Ties to Hazel McCallion Takes Office in Mississauga
items.summary: The Toronto Star reports that Alvin Tedjo's win in Mississauga's mayoral race carries a historical first: he is the city's first mayor since 1978 who never served under, or was, longtime mayor Hazel McCallion. According to the newspaper, Tedjo's victory over incumbent Carolyn Parrish and her predecessor Bonnie Crombie came with a wider margin than first reported, more than 20,000 votes ahead of Parrish and 30,000 ahead of Crombie with nearly all polls counted. The Star reports a University of Toronto Mississauga student and Tedjo supporter, Jan Durkiewicz, celebrated on election night by saying the polls had underestimated their campaign. According to the outlet, Tedjo, 43, said the result showed residents were ready for someone new and pledged to freeze the city's portion of property taxes for the next two years. The Star notes Tedjo will now lead the same council he first joined as a councillor four years ago.

items.title: City Puts Extra Bylaw Officers on Patrol as Mississauga Residents Mark Diwali With Fireworks
items.summary: The City of Mississauga reports it is reminding residents to plan ahead if fireworks will be part of their Diwali celebrations this year. According to the city, Diwali, also known as the Festival of Lights, is celebrated by many Mississauga residents and is often marked with gatherings, decorations, diyas, candles and fireworks. The city says anyone planning certain fireworks activities needs a permit, and residents are urged to follow the rules to prevent injuries, fires and property damage. According to the city, Municipal By-law Enforcement will have extra officers on duty during Diwali to help keep celebrations safe for residents and their neighbours alike. The city asks residents not to call 911 over fireworks complaints unless there is an immediate danger, such as a fire or someone being hurt.

items.title: Every Returning Councillor Who Ran Again Kept Their Seat as Mississauga Picked a New Mayor
items.summary: Insauga.com reports that while Mississauga voters chose change at the mayor's office, they kept every sitting city councillor who sought another term. According to the outlet, the only new faces on council when it convenes in mid-November will fill the wards 2 and 7 seats vacated by Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla, both of whom ran for mayor instead. The outlet reports Tedjo's winning tally reached 74,479 votes, ahead of incumbent Mayor Carolyn Parrish's 51,853 and former mayor Bonnie Crombie's 43,191, while Damerla finished fourth with 11,500 votes. According to insauga.com, ten other mayoral candidates also appeared on the ballot but drew far fewer votes than the top four finishers. The outlet reports the City of Mississauga said late Monday night that all polls had reported, though the results remain unofficial pending further confirmation.
